title: What AI Can't Do
about: Why sounding sure isn't the same as being right, and when to check.

cards.prompt: AI answers are **predictions**: best guesses, not checked facts. You're using one to write about your town's bridge.

steps.text: The AI says the bridge opened in **1952**, and sounds very sure. What do you do?

choices.text: Write it down: it sounds completely certain
choices.consequence: A reader writes in: it opened years later. Confident isn't the same as correct.

choices.text: Check a trusted source, like a history book
choices.consequence: Good thinking. Let's see what it says.

choices.text: Ask the AI if it's really sure it's right
choices.consequence: It says "Yes, I'm sure!" But an AI can't be sure its own answer is right.

steps.text: The local history book says **1958**. What now?

choices.text: Use 1958: the date from the history book
choices.consequence: Right: you checked a trusted source and caught the AI's mistake.

choices.text: Use 1952: the AI has read far more books
choices.consequence: Reading a lot doesn't check each answer. The book's date was checked by people.

cards.hint: The AI's answer is a guess. How could you find out whether it's right?
cards.explanation: Even a confident AI answer is a **prediction** and can be wrong, and asking it again doesn't help. Check important facts with a **trusted source**.

cards.prompt: A chatbot calmly says a film came out in 2009, but it was 2011. Why can AI sound sure yet be wrong?

options.text: It predicts from patterns and can't check the truth
It's trying to fool you on purpose, to seem clever
options.nudge: AI doesn't have plans or feelings. How does it make an answer?

options.text: It only sounds sure when right, so it misread you
options.nudge: Sounding sure doesn't come from being right. What is every AI answer?

options.text: It used its list of facts, which was out of date
options.nudge: A model has no list of facts: it learned patterns. So what is each answer?

cards.hint: What is every answer an AI gives you: a fact, or something else?
cards.explanation: Every answer is a **prediction** from patterns, never checked for truth, so it sounds just as sure when wrong. It isn't lying or reading a fact list.

cards.title: A program, not a person
cards.body:
A chatbot can sound caring, but can't notice if you're not OK.

If something's worrying you, talk to a **trusted adult** or a friend. In Australia, call **Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800)**, free, any time, up to age 25, or **Lifeline (13 11 14)**, any time, for anyone. In danger right now? Call **000**.

cards.prompt: Your photo app sorts pictures by who's in them.

steps.text: It labels your friend as someone else, and suggests sharing the photo with them. What do you do?

choices.text: Share it: the app is usually right about faces
choices.consequence: Now someone else has your friend's photo. Apps can mislabel faces, so check first.

choices.text: Fix the label, and don't share the photo
choices.consequence: Good: you caught the mistake before it spread. Face matching is a prediction.

choices.text: Keep the label: the app knows your friend's face
choices.consequence: Seeing a face often doesn't make every match right. This prediction is wrong.

cards.hint: The label is a prediction. What do you do with one before acting on it?
cards.explanation: Face matching is a **prediction**, so it can mislabel people. Check before acting: fix the label and don't share. The app is still useful, just not always right.

cards.prompt: Small jobs are fine for AI; big decisions about people need a **person**. Sort each job.
cards.hint: Ask: if the AI got it wrong, would someone be hurt or treated unfairly?
cards.nudge: Look again at jobs where a mistake would really affect someone's life.
cards.explanation: Spelling, photos and songs are low-stakes: mistakes are easy to fix. Punishments, treatment and jobs are **big decisions about people**, so a person must decide.

cards.prompt: Match each AI limit to an example of it.

pairs.right: Calls a yellow apple a banana
Tags your friend as someone else
An AI decides a student's punishment

cards.hint: Each example is from this module. Which limit explains what went wrong?
cards.nudge: Was each problem missing examples, false confidence, a wrong face match, or a big decision?
cards.explanation: Yellow apple: it **only knows its examples**. Wrong year: it **sounds sure when wrong**. Photo tag: it **can mislabel people**. Punishment: it **can't be responsible**.

cards.title: Recap
cards.body:
- AI gives **predictions**, not facts. Check important things.
- Big decisions about people need a person.
- Worried? Talk to a trusted adult, Kids Helpline (1800 55 1800) or Lifeline (13 11 14).

Next: the module quiz.
